The raw TOKEN count over the same range is 97 (grep -o); the 4 extra tokens sit on 4 two-token lines: 3288 (+1), 3290 (+1), 3294 (+1), 3511 (+1). _meta.source_anchor_convention: Bare 'app_command_interface.cpp:N' = src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp (the handler file, per the dispatch schema). Any other anchor is written repo-relative from the tree root.
schema_notes: `required` is tri-state: true = the command cannot act without the key on any path; false = optional on every path; "conditional" = required only inside a branch, the branch named in the key's `notes` and in the command's `branches`.

`branches` (unit-1 field, kept) -- most handlers in this unit are selector-shaped (`action`, `jump`, the first-non-empty ladders of `select`/`date`/`zoom`): a flat required/optional split would misstate them.
`value_docs` (unit-1 field, kept) -- where a key is enumerated and each value selects a different effect, C6's per-thing doc line is attached per value, not only per key.
`exclusive_groups` -- used here only where the code itself picks ONE of several spellings for the same quantity (moveto lat/latitude, lon/longitude, alt/altitude).

`downstream` (unit-1 field) -- not used in this unit: no handler in 3096-3944 forwards the whole `args` map. The one cross-handler hand-off is `media` -> `audio`, and it goes through a rebuilt COMMAND STRING, not through the map (:3511, recorded in media.notes).

Absent-key value for every eval* conversion is fixed IN the handler file and is not opaque: evalDouble("")=0.0, evalInt("")=0, evalString("")="" [app_command_interface.cpp:4458-4479]. What a NON-empty string evaluates to stays opaque here (app_command_eval.cpp, INTENT S5 item 5): recorded as evalDouble/evalInt/evalString, $-variable substitution possible.

Conversions that are NOT eval* are named with the function that does them (Utility::strToPosDouble, Utility::strToBool, Utility::isTrue, std::stod, FixedPointI16_2::fromString): those take the raw text, so no $-variable substitution happens on them.
_meta.other_args_uses_note: EMPTY, measured: every one of the 93 `args` occurrences in 3096-3944 is an `args[KEY]` read. No handler in this range calls args.begin()/args.end(), iterates the map, or forwards it. (Measured at b12c8cdd: `grep -n 'args' | awk '$1>=3096 && $1<=3944' | wc -l` = 93 = the `args[` line count.)

shared_context.executeCommandStatus: app_command_interface.cpp:1163-1177 -- the return path of every handler. debug_message EMPTY = success: `commandline` is recorded when recording is on and 'true' is returned. debug_message SET = two log lines ('Could not execute: <line>' + the message) and 'false'. A handler that returns without setting debug_message therefore reports SUCCESS even when it did nothing (three cases in this unit: mode with no `jump`, date sun with an unknown value, media's colour helper).
shared_context.args_container: stringHash_t = std::map<std::string,std::string> (src/tools/utility.hpp:85), member `args` (app_command_interface.hpp:204), cleared at the top of every executeCommand (app_command_interface.cpp:196-199). `args[KEY]` is std::map::operator[]: reading an ABSENT key INSERTS an empty entry. No handler in this unit walks the map, so the insertions are invisible here -- but `media` can re-enter executeCommand (:3511), which CLEARS and rebuilds `args` under the running handler (see media.notes).
shared_context.wait_channel: commandZoom is the one handler of this unit taking `uint64_t &wait` (:3268, dispatched at :297). The value is added to the script's own wait_time in milliseconds (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:306-331), i.e. it holds the SCRIPT, not the view.

select.doc: Choose the object the program points at and describes -- a star, a body of the solar system, a deep-sky object or a constellation.

hp.doc: The number of a star in the Hipparcos star catalogue.
hp.value: int (read with std::istringstream in the receiver, not evaluated here)
hp.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
hp.notes: A number no star answers to selects nothing and reports success (Core::selectObject returns 0, src/coreModule/core.cpp:1081-1089).

star.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried

planet.doc: The name of a body of the solar system; the word home_planet means the body you are standing on.

value_docs.home_planet: whatever body you are standing on right now (its English name is looked up and used instead, app_command_interface.cpp:3117-3118)

planet.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
planet.notes: Names are matched against both body trees, the old one first (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1040-1045).

body.doc: Another spelling of `planet`: the name of a body of the solar system.
body.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
body.notes: Handled exactly like `planet` (the same select_type W_PLANET is used, :3120), so the two spellings differ only in which is tried first: `planet` wins when both are on the line.

nebula.doc: The name of a deep-sky object (a galaxy, a nebula or a cluster).
nebula.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried

constellation.doc: The short name of a constellation to select, or the word zodiac to select the twelve constellations of the zodiac at once.
constellation.value: string (a constellation short name), or the word zodiac

value_docs.zodiac: select the twelve zodiac constellations together: Ari, Tau, Gem, Cnc, Leo, Vir, Sco, Sgr, Cap, Aqr, Psc, Lib (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1100-1117)

constellation.default: absent or empty -> the next identity key is tried
constellation.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3103-3106 (zodiac) and 3127-3129 (one constellation) -> src/coreModule/core.cpp:1052-1058 (W_CONSTELLATION="constellation", base_command_interface.hpp:97; W_ZODIAC="zodiac", base_command_interface.hpp:274)
constellation.notes: The short name is matched without regard to case (src/coreModule/constellation_mgr.cpp findFromAbbreviation uppercases both sides). Selecting a constellation clears the selected OBJECT (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1057-1058), so nothing is described afterwards.

constellation_star.doc: The short name of a constellation whose brightest star should be selected -- the way to centre the view on a constellation.
constellation_star.default: absent or empty -> nothing is selected: "command 'select' : no object found"

pointer.doc: Say off to select the object without drawing the marker around it.
values: off-forms per Utility::isFalse ("0", "off", "false", case-insensitive; src/tools/utility.hpp:172-183) = no marker
anything else, and absent = the marker is drawn
pointer.default: absent -> the marker is turned ON (isFalse("") is false, so the else branch runs)
pointer.notes: Read AFTER the object has been chosen, and only on the path that chose one: the `constellation zodiac` form returns at :3105 and the no-object form at :3135, so `pointer` does nothing on either. It has the last word over the marker handling inside the selection code (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2291, 2296).

branches.effect: select the twelve zodiac constellations and return; `pointer` is not read

branches.selector: first non-empty of hp, star, planet, body, nebula, constellation, constellation_star
branches.effect: select that object, then show or hide the marker

branches.selector: none of the seven identity keys
branches.effect: "command 'select' : no object found"

notes: The seven identity keys are tried in a FIXED order written into the code -- hp, star, planet, body, nebula, constellation, constellation_star (:3108-3132) -- and the first one present wins, whatever order the author wrote them in. The zodiac test comes before all of them (:3103).
Selecting something stops the view from following what it was following (Core::selectObject sets tracking off, src/coreModule/core.cpp:1081-1087).

deselect.doc: Undo a selection: drop one constellation from it, or clear everything that is selected.

constellation.doc: The short name of the one constellation to drop from the selection; leave it out to clear the whole selection.
constellation.default: absent or empty -> everything selected is cleared: the object, the constellations, the stars and the deep-sky objects (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1154-1160)
constellation.notes: Matched without regard to case; a name no constellation answers to changes nothing (src/coreModule/constellation_mgr.cpp findFromAbbreviation returns nullptr).

notes: This command never reports an error: with or without a key, right or wrong name, it always succeeds (:3156).

comment.registration: NOT in m_commands: literal string compare before the table lookup (app_command_interface.cpp:215-216). Confirms parse_model.pre_table_commands.
comment.doc: Start a skipped block: the lines after this one are read but not carried out, until an 'uncomment' line.

key_grammar.doc: This command takes no key. Anything written after it is parsed as key/value pairs and ignored.
key_grammar.key_domain: none -- the handler reads no key

notes: The whole handler is `swapCommand = true` (:3162), the flag the executor tests before dispatching anything: while it is set, every command is skipped and logged 'this command has not been executed' (executeCommand :225-228, field declared app_command_interface.hpp:206).

Because `comment`, `uncomment` and `struct` are compared BEFORE the skip test (:215-222 vs :225), those three still act inside a skipped block -- which is what makes the block closable at all. A second `comment` inside a block changes nothing.

The skip state belongs to the interface, not to the file: it is cleared at construction (:72) and by `script action end` (:2809, unit 2), and reaching the end of a script runs exactly that (terminateScript :178-181 <- src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:335). So a block left open at the end of a script does not leak into the next one.
Being outside m_commands also means the did-you-mean suggester can never propose these two names (parse_model.pre_table_commands).
There is one more `unskippable` escape: `terminateScript` sets it (:180) so the closing `script action end` runs even inside a skipped block (:225).

uncomment.registration: NOT in m_commands: literal string compare before the table lookup (app_command_interface.cpp:218-219). Confirms parse_model.pre_table_commands.
uncomment.doc: End a block started by 'comment': the lines after this one are carried out again.

key_grammar.doc: This command takes no key. Anything written after it is parsed as key/value pairs and ignored.
key_grammar.key_domain: none -- the handler reads no key

notes: The whole handler is `swapCommand = false` (:3169). An 'uncomment' with no 'comment' before it is legal and does nothing.
It does NOT close the other skip state: `struct if`'s own flag (ifSwap) is tested in the same condition (:225) and is cleared by its own commands, not by this one.

look_at.doc: Turn the view towards a given direction, or nudge it a little from where it points now.

azimuth.doc: Where to look, measured around the horizon in degrees.
azimuth.default: absent or empty -> the turn-to form is not taken (it needs `altitude` as well) and the nudge form is tried instead
azimuth.notes: Degrees: the receiver multiplies by PI/180 (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:149-150).

altitude.doc: Where to look, measured up from the horizon in degrees.
altitude.default: absent or empty -> the turn-to form is not taken and the nudge form is tried instead

duration.doc: How many seconds the turn takes.
duration.default: in the turn-to form, absent -> 1 second (the default argument of CoreLink::lookAt, src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:375); in the nudge form, absent -> 0, i.e. the view jumps at once

delta_azimuth.doc: How far to nudge the view around the horizon -- in RADIANS, not degrees (half a turn is about 3.14).
delta_azimuth.default: absent or empty -> 0, no nudge around; with `delta_altitude` also absent the command reports "Command 'look_at': wrong argument"
delta_azimuth.notes: [derived] Radians: the value is added to an angle that comes out of Utility::rectToSphe, which returns radians (src/tools/utility.cpp:102-107; use at src/navModule/navigator.cpp:186-193) -- no PI/180 anywhere on this path, unlike `azimuth`. It is SUBTRACTED from the current azimuth (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:193), so its sign is the opposite of `azimuth`'s direction.

delta_altitude.doc: How far to nudge the view up or down -- in RADIANS, not degrees (a quarter turn is about 1.57).
delta_altitude.default: absent or empty -> 0, no nudge up or down
delta_altitude.notes: [derived] Radians, same reasoning as `delta_azimuth`. The result is kept between straight down and straight up (src/navModule/navigator.cpp:195-197).

branches.effect: turn the view to that direction over `duration` seconds (1 by default), then return -- the delta keys are never read
nudge the view by those amounts; stops the view following whatever it was following (src/coreModule/core.hpp:266)
"Command 'look_at': wrong argument"

notes: The turn-to form needs BOTH `azimuth` and `altitude`: with only one of them the command falls through to the nudge form and, with no delta key, reports 'wrong argument' -- the given key is silently dropped.

The two forms use different units for the same kind of quantity (degrees for `azimuth`/`altitude`, radians for `delta_azimuth`/`delta_altitude`) and different absent-defaults for `duration` (1 second against 0).

star_lines.doc: Draw straight lines between named stars -- the stick figures of the constellations -- from a file or from one line of text.

action.doc: The only thing this can say is drop: erase every star line being drawn.

value_docs.drop: erase all the star lines drawn so far

action.default: absent or any other value -> the other keys are tried

load.doc: A file of star-line records to draw; what it contains replaces whatever was drawn.
load.value: string (a file name inside the script folder)
load.default: absent or empty -> the next key is tried
load.notes: The name is ALWAYS joined to the script folder (:3213), so an absolute path cannot be given. Inside the file, a line whose first character is '#' is skipped (src/coreModule/starLines.cpp:240) and each other line is one record of the shape described under `asterism`. Loading REPLACES what was drawn (the list is emptied first, src/coreModule/starLines.cpp:236). A file that cannot be opened is logged and the command still reports success (src/coreModule/starLines.cpp:230-233).

asterism.doc: One star-line record given directly on the line: a name, then how many segments follow, then that many pairs of star catalogue numbers.
asterism.value: string -- several words, so it has to be written between double quotes
asterism.notes: The record contains spaces, so it must be quoted or the parser will read only its first word (parse_model.quoting; the rest of the line becomes further key/value pairs). Shape: <name> <number of segments> then two Hipparcos numbers per segment (src/coreModule/starLines.cpp:258-268). Unlike `load` this ADDS to what is already drawn. A catalogue number that is 0, or that no star answers to, is logged and that segment is skipped (src/coreModule/starLines.cpp:270-287).

branches.effect: erase the star lines and return
read the file and replace what is drawn
add the lines of that one record
"Command 'star_lines': wrong argument"

notes: The three forms are tried in the order action, load, asterism, each returning at once (:3210, 3214, 3218), so only one acts per line.
`action` accepts only 'drop': any other value falls through to `load` without a word.

galaxy_stars.doc: Read the catalogue of stars that is drawn around you when you travel inside the galaxy.

load.doc: The catalogue file to read; it replaces the stars drawn before.
load.default: absent or empty -> "Command 'galaxy_stars': wrong argument. Use load filename"
load.notes: Three places are tried in order and the first that exists is used: the name as written (an absolute path, or one relative to the folder the program was started in), then inside the script folder, then inside the configuration folder (:3231-3239). If none exists the command reports "Command 'galaxy_stars': file not found: <name>". File shape: one star per line, a kind number then three coordinates; a line whose kind is not 1 to 7 is skipped (src/inGalaxyModule/starGalaxy.cpp:232-259).

branches.selector: load non-empty and the file was found
branches.effect: replace the in-galaxy star catalogue
"Command 'galaxy_stars': file not found: <name>"
"Command 'galaxy_stars': wrong argument. Use load filename"

notes: This is the only command of the unit whose file name may be an absolute path or relative to the working directory: the others join the script folder unconditionally.

position.doc: Remember where and when you are, in one single bookmark, or go back to what was remembered.

action.doc: Whether to record the present view or to return to the recorded one.

value_docs.save: record the date, the field of view, the place you are looking from, the body you are on and which scale you are in
value_docs.load: go back to what was recorded

action.default: absent or any other value -> "Command 'position': unknown parameter"

notes: One bookmark only, held in memory and lost when the program stops: date, field of view, latitude, longitude, altitude, home body, current scale (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.hpp:45-56). This is NOT the `session` command, which writes a file.

`load` before any `save` skips the place-and-date part (the recorded date is 0, src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:49) but still runs the last two lines: it asks for an empty body name and puts you back in the solar-system scale (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:75-76, the struct's defaults).
The place is read from, and restored to, the path that actually draws (src/coreModule/backup_mgr.cpp:59-73, 82-90) -- the same seam `moveto` uses.

zoom.signature: commandZoom(uint64_t &wait) -- the `center` form writes the script's inter-command delay (dispatched at :297)
zoom.doc: Change how much sky the screen shows: zoom in on what is selected, go to a given width of view, or bring the selected object to the middle.

auto.doc: Zoom in on the object that is selected, or back out.
auto.value: enumerated (open set: any other word means zoom in)

value_docs.out: go back out one step: to the view around the object's satellites, or to the starting view
value_docs.initial: go all the way back to the starting width of view and the starting direction
value_docs.in: zoom in on the selected object (any word that is neither 'out' nor 'initial' does this, including the word 'in' itself)

auto.default: absent or empty -> the `fov`, `delta_fov` and `center` forms are tried instead
auto.notes: With nothing selected, zooming in does nothing (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1321) and zooming out goes to the starting view.

manual.doc: Say on to zoom by one step at a time instead of going straight to the object.
manual.default: absent or any non-on value -> off, the zoom goes straight to its target
manual.notes: It only has an effect while the display feature `manual_zoom` is on (families.flags; the test is `allow_manual_zoom && FlagManualZoom`). A step halves the width of view when zooming in and doubles it when zooming out. It is read on the `auto` form only, and 'initial' ignores it (:3281).

duration.doc: How many seconds the movement takes.
duration.value: on the `auto` form: number read as raw text and always made positive (Utility::strToPosDouble, src/tools/utility.cpp:420-429) -- NO $-variable substitution; on the `fov` and `center` forms: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible
duration.default: on `auto`, absent -> the application's own move duration (`set auto_move_duration`, src/coreModule/core.hpp:277-280); on `fov`, absent -> 0, the change is instant; on `center`, absent -> 5 seconds
duration.notes: The same key is read three times with two different converters -- a value like `$myvar` works after `fov` and `center` but not after `auto`, where it becomes 0. On `auto` a negative value is turned positive.

fov.doc: Go to a given width of view, in degrees -- how much sky the screen shows from edge to edge.
fov.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
fov.notes: The value that finally lands is kept between 0.0001 and 350 degrees (src/coreModule/projector.cpp:92-99; the upper bound is the one set by the configuration, default 350 at src/coreModule/projector.cpp:45).

delta_fov.doc: Widen (a positive number) or narrow (a negative number) the view by this many degrees, at once.
delta_fov.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
delta_fov.notes: Applied immediately with no smooth movement, and `duration` is not read on this form. The comment above it (:3291) records the author's own doubt about recording deltas.

center.doc: Say on to bring the selected object to the middle of the view.
center.value: the exact text 'on' and nothing else
center.default: absent, or any other value -> "Command 'zoom': unknown argument"
center.notes: Compared against the exact text 'on': '1', 'true', 'ON' and 'On' do NOT work here, unlike the on/off grammar used by `flag` and by `manual` just above. The view moves over the application's own move duration, while the SCRIPT waits `duration` seconds (5 by default).

branches.effect: zoom in on / out from the selected object
move the width of view to that many degrees

branches.selector: auto and fov absent, delta_fov non-empty
branches.effect: change the width of view at once
centre the selected object and hold the SCRIPT for `duration` seconds
"Command 'zoom': unknown argument"

notes: One form per line, in the fixed order auto, fov, delta_fov, center.

The `center` form is the only one that holds the script: `wait` is set to duration x 1000 milliseconds (:3296) and only when that is more than 0. Every other form returns at once while the view keeps moving on its own.
The `auto` form reads `duration` twice -- once as a positive number for every branch (:3270) and once as an emptiness test for the default (:3276).

timerate.doc: Change how fast time runs in the sky: give a speed, stop it, or step it up and down.

rate.doc: How many seconds of sky time pass for each second of real time: 1 is real time, 0 is frozen, a negative number runs time backwards.
rate.default: absent or empty -> the `action` forms are tried instead
rate.notes: The number is multiplied by one second expressed in days (JD_SECOND, src/coreModule/time_mgr.hpp:29) before it is stored. Giving `rate` without `duration` also lets time run again if it was stopped (:3313).

duration.doc: How many seconds to take easing into the new speed, instead of changing it at once.
duration.value: number read as raw text with std::stod -- NO $-variable substitution
duration.default: absent or empty -> the speed changes at once
duration.notes: On this path time is only let free again when the easing FINISHES (src/coreModule/time_mgr.cpp:34-38), unlike the instant form which frees it first. A value that is not a number stops the program -- see `flagged`.

action.doc: What to do to the flow of time when no speed is given.

value_docs.pause: stop time where it is -- or start it again if it is already stopped: this value FLIPS the state rather than only stopping (:3321)
value_docs.increment: make time run faster by one step (twice as fast unless `step` says otherwise)
value_docs.decrement: make time run slower by one step (half as fast unless `step` says otherwise)
value_docs.sincrement: make time run faster by a small step (1.05 times unless `step` says otherwise)
value_docs.sdecrement: make time run slower by a small step (1.05 times unless `step` says otherwise)

action.default: absent, or a value that is none of the six, and no `rate` -> "Command 'time_rate': unknown argument"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3306, 3319-3392 (W_PAUSE="pause", W_RESUME="resume", W_INCREMENT="increment", W_DECREMENT="decrement", W_SINCREMENT="sincrement", W_SDECREMENT="sdecrement": base_command_interface.hpp:160, 168, 86/145, 87/144, 275, 276)
action.notes: The four stepping values all let time run again first (:3328, 3346, 3361, 3377). Near zero they snap instead of multiplying: from stopped, one step up goes to real time and one step down to real time backwards (:3337-3338, 3370-3371).

step.doc: The number one step multiplies the speed by.
step.default: absent or empty -> 2 for increment and decrement, 1.05 for sincrement and sdecrement
step.notes: Read for the four stepping actions only; `pause` and `resume` ignore it.

branches.effect: let time run and set the speed at once
ease from the present speed to the new one over `duration` seconds
flip the stopped state / let time run
multiply or divide the speed by one step and rewrite the recorded line as an absolute speed

branches.selector: neither rate nor a known action
branches.effect: "Command 'time_rate': unknown argument"

notes: Recording rewrite (C1-relevant, same shape as `flag`'s): each of the four stepping actions replaces `commandline` with `timerate rate <the speed reached>` (:3341, 3358, 3374, 3390), so a recorded script replays the speed and not the step. The rewrite happens before executeCommandStatus records the line (:1167).
`sincrement`/`sdecrement` carry one more rule: when the speed is smaller than 3 in size and the observer is more than 150 million kilometres up, the speed is first set to +3 or -3 (:3348, 3379).
The error text says 'time_rate' though the command is spelled `timerate` (:3392).
flagged: timerate `duration`: `stod(argDuration)` at app_command_interface.cpp:3317 runs on the raw text and nothing in the call chain catches exceptions (checked at HEAD: the only `catch` in src/interfaceModule, src/scriptModule, src/mainModule and src/main.cpp is app_command_eval.cpp:151, on another path). `timerate rate 1 duration abc` therefore stops the program instead of reporting a script error. Same class as the unit-1 dso3d `depth` finding; the lint rule this suggests needs Vixy's word on severity. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope).

moveto.doc: Move the observer to another place on the body you are standing on, or to another height above it.

lat.doc: Where to go: how far north (a positive number) or south (a negative one) of the equator, in degrees.
lat.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or one of the two words below

value_docs.default: the latitude the program starts at (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:884-886)
value_docs.inverse: the same latitude on the other side of the equator (the present value with its sign turned round)

lat.default: absent or empty -> `latitude` is read instead; if that is empty too, the latitude you are at now is kept

latitude.doc: The same thing as `lat`, spelled out.
latitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default / inverse
latitude.default: absent or empty -> the latitude you are at now is kept
latitude.notes: Read only when `lat` is empty (:3407), so `lat` wins when both are on the line.

lon.doc: Where to go: how far east (a positive number) or west (a negative one), in degrees.
lon.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or one of the two words below

value_docs.default: the longitude the program starts at (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:888-890)
value_docs.inverse: half a turn round the body: the present longitude plus 180 degrees

lon.default: absent or empty -> `longitude` is read instead; if that is empty too, the longitude you are at now is kept

longitude.doc: The same thing as `lon`, spelled out.
longitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default / inverse
longitude.default: absent or empty -> the longitude you are at now is kept

alt.doc: How high to stand above the body, in metres; a value that starts with + or - is added to your present height instead of replacing it.
alt.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or the word default

value_docs.default: the height the program starts at (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:892-894)

alt.default: absent or empty -> `altitude` is read instead; if that is empty too, the height you are at now is kept
alt.notes: The word `inverse` is NOT accepted here, unlike `lat` and `lon`. The + / - test looks at the first character of the text (:3438), so it is the written sign that matters, not the value: `alt +0` is relative, `alt 5` is not.

altitude.doc: The same thing as `alt`, spelled out.
altitude.value: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible -- or default, or a value starting with + or -
altitude.default: absent or empty -> the height you are at now is kept

delta_lat.doc: How many degrees to move north (positive) or south (negative) from where the move already puts you.

delta_lon.doc: How many degrees to move east (positive) or west (negative) from where the move already puts you.

delta_alt.doc: How many metres to rise (positive) or drop (negative) from the height the move already puts you at.

multiply_alt.doc: Multiply the height by this number -- 2 puts you twice as high, 0.5 half as high.
multiply_alt.notes: Applied AFTER `delta_alt` (:3451-3456), so the two compose in that order whatever the order on the line.

duration.doc: How many seconds the move takes; leave it out to arrive at once.
duration.notes: Turned into whole milliseconds (:3458), so anything under a thousandth of a second is the same as 0.

branches.selector: at least one of lat/latitude, lon/longitude, alt/altitude, delta_lat, delta_lon, delta_alt, multiply_alt
branches.effect: work out the target place from the present one, then move there over `duration`
"command 'move_to' : missing lat && lon && alt"

notes: The target is built in a fixed order: start from where you are now, replace with `lat`/`lon`/`alt` if given, then add the delta keys, then multiply the height (:3416-3456). The order written on the line never matters.
The emptiness test at :3412 counts the SHORT spellings only after they have absorbed the long ones (:3407-3409), so `moveto latitude 45` is enough on its own.

The place the move starts from is the place the drawn path reports, which is not always the one the old observer holds (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:836-852): after a `camera action descend`, `delta_alt` and `multiply_alt` compute from the camera's height.

What lands is clamped differently on the two paths: the old observer holds latitude within +/-90 degrees and never goes below 0.1 metre of height (src/navModule/observer.cpp:61-64), the camera clamps nothing (recorded in src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:850-852, not a thing this command decides).
The error text spells the command 'move_to' though the command is `moveto` (:3413).

mode.doc: Jump between the four scales the program can show: the solar system, the stars around it, the galaxy, and the universe.

jump.value: enumerated, matched without regard to case

value_docs.in_solarsystem: the scale of the solar system, seen from a body or from space near one (spelling 'insolarsystem' does the same)
value_docs.in_stellarsystem: the scale of another star's system (spelling 'instellarsystem' does the same)
value_docs.in_galaxy: the scale of the galaxy around the solar system (spelling 'ingalaxy' does the same)
value_docs.in_universe: the scale of the universe beyond the galaxy (spelling 'inuniverse' does the same)

jump.default: absent or empty -> the command does NOTHING AT ALL and still reports success: `body` and `altitude` are inside the same test (:3468-3486)
jump.notes: The value is put into lower case before it is compared (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:86), so IN_GALAXY works too. A value that is none of the eight does not report an error and does not stay put either: the present scale is left and re-entered and whatever was selected is dropped (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:88, 101-103).

body.doc: Which body to stand on after the jump; the word selected means the object selected right now.
body.value: string (a body's English name), or the word selected
body.default: absent or empty -> you stay on the body you are on
body.notes: Read only when `jump` is present. A name no body answers to leaves you where you are (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2087).

altitude.doc: How high to stand after the jump, in metres; a value starting with + or - is added to your present height instead.
altitude.default: absent or empty -> your height is unchanged
altitude.notes: Read only when `jump` is present. The move is immediate (the duration passed is 0, :3484). The + / - test looks at the first character of the text (:3480), exactly as `moveto alt` does.

branches.effect: change scale, then optionally the body you stand on, then optionally your height
nothing happens; no message is set, so the command reports SUCCESS and is recorded

notes: `mode body Mars` or `mode altitude 1000` on their own do nothing whatever: both keys live inside the `jump` test.

The name `mode` is also one of the 43 setting names (`set mode <value>`), which is recorded as parsing, reporting success and calling nothing (families.set_names.known_defective). The two are unrelated surfaces with the same spelling.
Changing scale always drops the selection, even when the scale does not actually change (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:101-102).

media.doc: Play a video in the dome -- or a sound on its own -- and control it while it plays.

action.doc: What to do with the video.

value_docs.play: start a video (all the other keys below belong to this one)
value_docs.stop: stop the video that is playing
value_docs.pause: hold the video where it is, or let it go on if it is already held (src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp pauseCurrentVideo)
value_docs.jump: move within the video by the number of seconds in `value`
value_docs.restart: start the video again from its beginning

action.default: absent, or a value that is none of the five -> only `speed`, `speed_increment` and `subtitle` are looked at; with none of those, "command 'media': unknown parameter"
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3492-3495, 3738-3750 (W_ACTION="action", W_PLAY="play", W_STOP="stop", W_PAUSE="pause", W_JUMP="jump", W_RESTART="restart": base_command_interface.hpp:81, 158, 271, 160, 282, 283)

type.value: enumerated, matched without regard to case

value_docs.vr360: wrapped on a sphere all around you -- a 360-degree video
value_docs.vrcube: wrapped on a cube all around you -- a cube-map video
value_docs.image: as a picture object in the sky, placed by `name` and `position`
value_docs.dual_viewport: flat, in the two-part screen arrangement

type.default: absent, or a value that is none of the five -> if `audioname` is given the whole command becomes an `audio` command (see notes); otherwise "Command 'media' argument action need argument 'type'"
type.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3507-3515 -> src/mediaModule/media.cpp:48-71 (W_TYPE="type", base_command_interface.hpp:119; W_VR360="vr360", W_VRCUBE="vrcube": base_command_interface.hpp:278, 279)
type.notes: Matched without regard to case (src/mediaModule/media.cpp:65) -- but the folder the file is looked for in is decided by comparing the value AS TYPED against 'vr360'/'vrcube' (:3521): `type VR360` plays as a 360-degree video while the file is looked for in the ordinary media folder instead of the vr360 one.

videoname.default: absent -> the empty name is looked up, is not found, and the command reports "command 'media': file videoname not found"
videoname.notes: Looked for in the vr360 folder when the value of `type` was written exactly 'vr360' or 'vrcube', and in the media folder otherwise (:3520-3526). The name is also the base for the two `auto` forms of `subtitlename` and `audioname`: its extension is replaced by '-<language>' (:3541-3551), and a name with no extension at all makes those two forms impossible (a warning is logged).

audioname.doc: A sound file to play in step with the video; the word auto asks for the one named after the video with the sky language added.
audioname.value: string (a file name), or the word auto

value_docs.auto: use <the video's name>-<sky language>.ogg from the media folder, if that file exists (:3637-3647)

audioname.default: absent -> no separate sound is played
audioname.notes: A name whose seventh character from the end is '-' (like film-en.ogg) is looked up again with the current sky language put in its place, and the name as written is used if that fails (:3653-3669). With NO `type` on the line, this key alone turns the command into `audio filename <name> action play loop <loop>` (:3510-3511).

name.doc: The name to give the picture when `type` is image, so that other commands can find it afterwards.
name.notes: Only used when `type` is image: it names the picture object, and the see-through keys use it to find that picture again (:3701, 3708, 3721, 3729). Loading a picture under a name that already exists replaces it (src/mediaModule/image_mgr.cpp:61).

position.doc: What a `type image` video is fixed to.
position.value: enumerated, matched without regard to case

value_docs.viewport: fixed to the screen, so it does not move when the view turns
value_docs.horizontal: fixed to your horizon, so it stays over the same part of the landscape
value_docs.equatorial: fixed to the sky, so it follows the stars as they turn
value_docs.j2000: fixed to the sky as it stood in the year 2000, the frame catalogues use
value_docs.spherical: wrapped as a sphere around you

position.default: absent, or any word that is none of the six -> viewport (src/mediaModule/image_mgr.cpp:73-82)

project.doc: How many copies of a `type image` video are drawn around the dome.
project.value: enumerated (anything not listed means one copy)

value_docs.twice: two copies, half a turn apart (0 and 180 degrees)
value_docs.thrice: three copies, a third of a turn apart (0, 120 and 240 degrees)

project.default: absent or any other value -> one copy
project.notes: Compared as typed, so 'Twice' means one copy. Only used when `type` is image.

pause.doc: Say true to start the video already held on its first frame instead of playing.
pause.value: boolean (Utility::strToBool: only 'true' and '1', without regard to case; src/tools/utility.cpp:432-445)
pause.default: absent -> false, the video starts playing
pause.notes: A narrower on/off grammar than `loop` just below it: 'on' is NOT accepted here. Any separate sound file is held with the video.

loop.doc: Say on to start the video again each time it reaches its end.
loop.value: boolean (on-forms per Utility::isTrue: "1", "on", "true", without regard to case)
loop.default: absent -> no looping (the handler turns it off explicitly, :3503-3505)

subtitlename.doc: The subtitle file to show with the video; the word auto asks for the one named after the video in the subtitle language.
subtitlename.value: string (a file name), or the word auto

value_docs.auto: use <the video's name>-<subtitle language>.srt from the media folder, if that file exists (:3557-3567)

subtitlename.default: absent -> any subtitles already loaded are dropped (:3607-3609)
subtitlename.notes: A name whose seventh character from the end is '-' (like film-en.srt) is looked up again with the current subtitle language put in its place, and the name as written is used if that fails (:3573-3589). When a file is found, the display feature 'subtitle' is forced on (:3601-3606). A file that is nowhere to be found is logged and the video still plays.

value_docs.toggle: show them if they are hidden, hide them if they are shown

subtitle.default: absent on an `action play` line -> subtitles are shown when a subtitle file was found and left alone otherwise (:3620-3623); absent on a line with no known action -> this form is not taken
subtitle.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3611-3623 (on an `action play` line) and 3762-3771 (on its own) (W_SUBTITLE="subtitle", W_TOGGLE="toggle": base_command_interface.hpp:165, 124)
subtitle.notes: The two places read the same key differently -- on its own, the toggle test looks at the value of `action`, not at this value (:3764). See `flagged`.

subtitle_project.doc: How many copies of the subtitles are drawn around the dome.
subtitle_project.value: enumerated (anything not listed means one copy)

value_docs.twice: two copies, at the front and the back (180 and 0 degrees)

subtitle_project.default: absent or any other value -> one copy (at 180 degrees)
subtitle_project.notes: Compared as typed. The angles are not the same ones `project` uses for pictures.

speed.doc: How fast to play: 1 is the normal speed, 2 twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast.
speed.value: number with at most two figures after the point (FixedPointI16_2, src/tools/fixed_point.hpp:2198) -- read as raw text, NO $-variable substitution
speed.default: absent on an `action play` line -> the normal speed 1 (:3687-3689); absent on a line with no known action -> this form is not taken
speed.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3684-3689 (on an `action play` line) and 3752-3756 (on its own) -> src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp:179-201 (W_SPEED="speed", base_command_interface.hpp:163)
speed.notes: Kept between 0.1 and 10; 0 or less is refused with a log line and nothing changes (src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp:181-196). Figures past the second decimal are dropped. While the speed is not exactly 1 the separate sound file is cut, and it starts again in step when the speed returns to 1 (src/mediaModule/media.hpp:428-441). A value containing anything but figures, a sign and one point stops the program -- see `flagged`.

speed_increment.doc: Add this to the playing speed -- a negative number slows it down.
speed_increment.value: number with at most two figures after the point (FixedPointI16_2) -- read as raw text, NO $-variable substitution
speed_increment.default: absent -> this form is not taken
speed_increment.notes: The sum is kept between 0.1 and 10 like `speed`. Only read on a line with no known `action`, and only when `speed` is not also there (:3752-3757).

value.doc: For `action jump`: how many seconds to move within the video -- forward if positive, back if negative.
value.default: absent -> 0, the video does not move
value.notes: Jumping back past the beginning starts the video again (src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp:692-695); jumping past the end does nothing (src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp:696).

color_value.doc: The colour to make see-through in the video, written in one word: x followed by six hexadecimal figures, or the three numbers 0-255 run together after the letters r, g and b.
color_value.default: absent -> the r/g/b keys are used instead; with none of them nothing about the see-through colour changes
color_value.notes: Same spelling of colours as the `illuminate` command uses, and the same key name.

r.doc: How much red in the colour to make see-through, from 0 to 1.
r.default: absent -> 0 when either of g or b is given; all three absent and `color_value` absent -> nothing about the see-through colour changes

g.doc: How much green in the colour to make see-through, from 0 to 1.

b.doc: How much blue in the colour to make see-through, from 0 to 1.

intensity.doc: How far a colour may differ from the chosen one and still be made see-through.
intensity.default: absent -> 0.05 (the default of Media::setKeyColor / Media::imageSetKeyColor, src/mediaModule/media.hpp:128, 299)
intensity.notes: Read only when a colour was successfully read from `color_value` or from r/g/b (:3697).

keycolor.doc: Say on to make the chosen colour see-through while the video plays, off to stop doing that.
keycolor.value: boolean (on-forms per Utility::isTrue; anything else = off)
keycolor.notes: For every type but image, switching it on also switches the fading off (:3725, src/mediaModule/media.hpp:121-123).

branches.selector: action play, no usable type, audioname given
branches.effect: the line is rebuilt as `audio filename <audioname> action play loop <loop>` and run instead

branches.selector: action play, no usable type, no audioname
branches.effect: "Command 'media' argument action need argument 'type'"

branches.selector: action play with a usable type
branches.effect: load the subtitles, load the sound, play the video, then apply speed, see-through colour and transparency
stop the video
hold the video, or let it go on
move within the video by `value` seconds
play the video again from its beginning
change the speed of the video that is playing
add to the speed of the video that is playing
show or hide the subtitles
"command 'media': unknown parameter"

notes: The colour keys, `keycolor` and `speed` are read on the `action play` path only (except `speed`, which has a second reading of its own at :3752): the see-through colour of a video that is already playing cannot be changed.
Colour errors are deliberately swallowed here: when the colour helper reports one, the message is thrown away (:3714-3715) and the video plays unchanged.

C1-relevant, the audio-only path (:3511): the handler calls executeCommand again from inside itself, and that call CLEARS and refills `args` and replaces `commandline` (:196-199). Two consequences: nothing after :3511 may read `args` (nothing does -- the call is returned immediately), and a recording of `media action play audioname x` stores the rebuilt `audio ...` line instead of the line the author wrote (executeCommandStatus :1167).

Also C1-relevant at :3511: the rebuilt line ends with 'loop ' when `loop` is absent -- a key with no value, which the parser silently drops (parse_model.pair_extraction). And an audio file name containing spaces cannot survive the rebuild, because the quotes were already stripped when the line was parsed.
`action play` needs the video file to exist even when `type` is image: the picture is a video texture (:3526-3530, src/mediaModule/media.cpp:219-222).
The five actions each return at once, so no line can both play and stop.
flagged: media `subtitle` on its own (app_command_interface.cpp:3762-3771): the toggle test at :3764 reads `argAction`, not `argSubtitle`. `media subtitle toggle` therefore does NOT flip the subtitles -- 'toggle' is not an on-form, so it HIDES them -- while `media action toggle subtitle <anything>` flips them. The `action play` reading of the same key (:3613) does it correctly. Which of the two is the intended spelling decides what the editor documents and completes: Vixy. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope).

media `speed` / `speed_increment`: FixedPointI16_2::fromString throws on any character that is not a figure, a sign or a point, and on more than one point (src/tools/fixed_point.hpp:397-421, with THROW_ON_FIXED_POINT_ERROR = 1 at src/tools/fixed_point.hpp:12); nothing in the call chain catches it (same check as for timerate). `media speed fast`, or `media speed $var`, therefore stops the program. Same class as the unit-1 dso3d `depth` finding; lint severity needs Vixy. Recorded, not fixed.

domemasters.doc: Save what the dome is showing as an image file: one picture, or a whole sequence of them.

action.doc: Whether to save one picture now or to start (or stop) saving a sequence.

value_docs.snapshot: save one picture of the dome now
value_docs.record: start saving one picture per frame -- or stop, if a sequence is already being saved: this value FLIPS the state (src/appModule/save_screen_interface.cpp:96-102)

action.default: absent, or a value that is neither -> "command 'domemasters': unknown argument"
action.notes: A single picture is refused while a sequence is being saved (src/appModule/save_screen_interface.cpp:148-149) -- with no message, so the command still reports success. The file names are <base>-YY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS.png for a single picture and <base>-000000.png, -000001.png ... for a sequence, with .jpg instead of .png while the display feature 'image_compression_loss' is on (src/appModule/save_screen_interface.cpp:118-127, 347-360).

branches.effect: save one picture and return
start or stop saving a sequence and return

branches.selector: action present but neither word, or action absent
branches.effect: "command 'domemasters': unknown argument"

notes: DEFECT, recorded not fixed: the more precise message "Command 'domemasters': unknown action value" (:3792) can never be seen. Its branch does not return, and the next line overwrites the message with "command 'domemasters': unknown argument" (:3794). A wrong value and a missing key are therefore reported identically.
Only the square dome-master picture is written, not the whole window (src/appModule/save_screen_interface.cpp:156-167).

date.doc: Set the date and time the sky is showing, either outright or by moving it along.

jday.doc: The date given as a Julian day -- the running count of days astronomers use, where the whole number changes at noon.
jday.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
jday.notes: The date that lands is kept inside the range the ephemerides can serve (src/coreModule/time_mgr.cpp:45-46). The half-day offset the doc line mentions -- the whole number changing at noon and not at midnight -- is written into the conversion itself (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:239-244).

local.doc: The date and time written out, read as the time on your own clock.
local.value: text of the shape [+/-]YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss -- the T is a letter you write; a value starting with T sets the time only and keeps the day
local.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; a value that cannot be read -> "Error parsing date local"
local.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3810-3828 -> src/appModule/space_date.cpp:255-279 (reading), 579-594 (the day the T-form keeps) (W_LOCAL="local", base_command_interface.hpp:219)
local.notes: How the text is actually read (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:265): a number, then ONE character of any kind, then the next number, and so on -- so 2020/01/01T00:00:00 is read just as happily as the dashes-and-colons form. A value with no time part is read as that day at 00:00:00. The month must be 1 to 12, the day 1 to 31 (whatever the month), the hour 0 to 23, the minutes and seconds 0 to 59; anything else is refused. The value is then moved by the program's time-zone setting to get the sky's own time (:3823).

utc.doc: The date and time written out, read as universal time (the time at longitude zero) instead of your own.
utc.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; a value that cannot be read -> "Error parsing date utc"
utc.notes: Same reading as `local` but with no time-zone step, and there is no T-only form here: a value starting with T is refused.

relative.doc: Move the date on by this many days of the body you are standing on -- its own day, which is not always 24 hours.
relative.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative.notes: The body's own day is used unless it is longer than 366 of our days, in which case one of our days is used instead (:3852). Standing nowhere -- in the galaxy or the universe view -- the command reports an error (:3847-3850, the message is in French in the source).

relative_year.doc: Move the date on by this many years, keeping the same month, day and time.
relative_year.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative_year.notes: The year number is simply added, so a negative value goes back.

relative_month.doc: Move the date on by this many months, keeping the same day and time.
relative_month.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
relative_month.notes: The month number is simply added, so 13 means a year and a month later (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2528).

sidereal.doc: Move the date on by this many turns of the body you are standing on with respect to the stars -- its sidereal day.
sidereal.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried
sidereal.notes: Like `relative`, the body's turn is used unless it is longer than 366 of our days (:3883), and standing nowhere gives an error (:3878-3881, French in the source).

load.doc: Take the date from the computer or from the program's own setting.

value_docs.current: set the sky to the computer's date and time right now
value_docs.preset: set the sky to the date the program is configured to start at -- but only when it is configured to start at a preset date, otherwise the computer's date is used (:3898-3900)
value_docs.keep_time: take today's date from the computer but keep the time of day the sky is already showing

load.default: absent or empty -> the next form is tried; any other value -> "Command 'date': unknown load value"
load.notes: The setting `preset` reads is the one `set startup_time_mode` writes (families.set_names), and the preset date itself is the configured start date (src/appModule/app.hpp:115-117).

sun.doc: Move the time to one of the Sun's moments of the day where you are standing.

value_docs.set: the time the Sun sets today at your place
value_docs.rise: the time the Sun rises today at your place
value_docs.meridian: the time the Sun is highest today -- local noon
value_docs.midnight: the opposite of local noon: the calculation is made half a world away and the answer moved on one day (:3933-3936)

sun.default: absent or empty -> "command 'date' : unknown argument"; any other value -> nothing happens and the command reports SUCCESS (see `flagged`)
sun.source: app_command_interface.cpp:3919-3940 -> src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:535-547 -> src/coreModule/time_mgr.cpp:62-158 (rise), 159-251 (set), 253-349 (meridian) (W_SUN="sun", W_SET="set", W_RISE="rise", W_MERIDIAN="meridian", W_MIDNIGHT="midnight": base_command_interface.hpp:126, 289, 290, 291, 292)
sun.notes: The calculation uses the longitude and latitude you are at. Where the Sun neither rises nor sets that day, the time goes to about local noon instead (time_mgr.cpp, the |Ho|>1 branch). If the calculation returns exactly zero the date is left alone (:3923, 3927, 3931, 3935 -- each carries the author's own TODO).

branches.selector: the first non-empty of jday, local, utc, relative, relative_year, relative_month, sidereal, load, sun
branches.effect: that one form acts and the command returns; the keys after it are never read
"command 'date' : unknown argument"

notes: The nine forms are tried in a fixed order written into the code (jday, local, utc, relative, relative_year, relative_month, sidereal, load, sun) and only the first one present acts, whatever the order on the line.

Sharp edge on the T-only form of `local`: the day it keeps comes from a text that begins with 'BC ' when the sky is at a year before 1 AD (src/appModule/space_date.cpp:587-593), so the first ten characters are not a date and the command reports 'Error parsing date local'. Only years before 1 AD are affected.

DEFECT, recorded not fixed: `date load preset` tests the same thing twice -- `getStartupTimeMode() == W_PRESET || getStartupTimeMode() == W_PRESET` (:3898). The startup path that this is plainly copied from tests the two spellings 'preset' and 'Preset' (src/appModule/app.cpp:656), and W_PRESET is only "preset" (base_command_interface.hpp:287). So with the setting written 'Preset' the program starts at the preset date but `date load preset` goes to the computer's date instead.
flagged: date `sun` with a value that is none of the four (app_command_interface.cpp:3937-3938): the line `_("Command 'date': unknown sun value");` translates a message and throws it away -- debug_message is never set, so `date sun banana` reports SUCCESS and is recorded. Same class as the unit-1 suntrace finding (a branch that reports success having done nothing). Whether this should become a lint error and with what severity: Vixy. Recorded, not fixed (out of scope).

c1_parse_model: CONFIRMS parse_model.pre_table_commands from the other side: commandComment/commandUncomment are two-line handlers that only move `swapCommand` (:3162, :3169), and the executor tests those literals BEFORE the skip test (:215-222 vs :225) -- which is what lets a block be closed at all. Adds the third escape the model does not mention: `unskippable` (:180, :229), set only by terminateScript so the closing `script action end` runs inside a skipped block.

ADDS to parse_model: a handler may RE-ENTER executeCommand. `media` does it at :3511 (the audio-only path), and executeCommand clears `args` and replaces `commandline` at :196-199. Consequences for scedit: (a) the recorded line for `media action play audioname x` is the rebuilt `audio ...` line, not what the author wrote; (b) the rebuilt line is built by string concatenation from values whose quotes were already stripped, so a file name with spaces is destroyed; (c) it ends with a dangling `loop` key when `loop` is absent, which the parser then drops silently (parse_model.pair_extraction) -- the drop is what makes it harmless.

CONFIRMS the recording-rewrite class found in unit 1 on `flag`: `timerate action increment|decrement|sincrement|sdecrement` rewrites `commandline` to `timerate rate <resulting speed>` (:3341, 3358, 3374, 3390) so a recording replays a state, not a step. Two of the four commands that rewrite their own line are now known; both are in the 'relative operation' family.

REFINES parse_model: the SAME key can carry a different value grammar in different branches of one handler. `zoom duration` is Utility::strToPosDouble on the `auto` branch (raw text, no $-substitution, sign discarded) and evalDouble on the `fov`/`center` branches (:3270 vs :3288, :3294). `media subtitle` and `media speed` likewise have two readings each (:3611/:3762, :3684/:3752). A tool that maps key -> value domain per COMMAND is not faithful; the mapping is per command AND branch.

REFINES parse_model.key_case's consequence for VALUES: value case is preserved by the parser, and handlers disagree about what to do with it. Matched case-insensitively: `mode jump` (src/executorModule/executor.cpp:86), `media type` (src/mediaModule/media.cpp:65), `media position` (src/mediaModule/image_mgr.cpp:76), constellation short names (constellation_mgr findFromAbbreviation). Matched exactly as typed: `zoom center` (only 'on'), `media project`/`media subtitle_project` (only 'twice'/'thrice'), every W_* comparison in `date`, `star_lines`, `position`, `timerate`. And `media type` is BOTH at once (:3521 compares the raw text while src/mediaModule/media.cpp:65 lowercases), which is a behaviour difference, not just a spelling one.

CONFIRMS the eval boundary recorded in unit 1 and widens the list of NON-eval converters that appear as value grammars: Utility::strToPosDouble (zoom), Utility::strToBool (media pause), Utility::isTrue (zoom manual, media loop/keycolor/subtitle), Utility::isFalse (select pointer), std::stod (timerate duration), FixedPointI16_2::fromString (media speed, speed_increment), std::istringstream (select hp, in the receiver). None of them substitutes $-variables, so 'does $var work here?' is a per-key fact, not a per-command one.
